paper_title: Developing Story Case Studies of Generative AI's Use in Journalism
caption: : The distribution of different input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs, over the WildChat conversations that are matched to online articles from the two identified news agencies.
model_annotation: This donut chart displays the distribution of different input stimulus material types provided by journalists to large language models, categorized under the central label "Stimulus Type." The chart contains 11 slices, each labeled with its category name and corresponding percentage displayed outside the ring. The largest slice is "Draft/Other" at 26.4%, shown in a dark red color and occupying the upper-right portion of the chart. The next two largest slices are "Press Release" at 18.7%, depicted in a golden-yellow color, and "External News Article" at 18.1%, shown in dark green, both positioned on the left side of the chart. "Interview" accounts for 8.8% and appears in a medium blue shade at the bottom of the chart. "Organizational Report" at 7.7% is rendered in a light pink or mauve color on the right side. "Event Posting" at 6.6% is shown in a dark brown or maroon hue, also on the right. "Intra-agency news article" and "Organizational Website" each represent 4.9%, displayed in a lighter blue and a dark navy color, respectively, at the bottom portion. "Email" at 2.7% appears as a light green slice on the left, and "Social Media Post" at 1.1% is the smallest slice, shown in a muted olive or dark yellow tone at the top. The percentage labels are placed adjacent to each slice outside the ring rather than inside. The slices appear to be arranged roughly in descending order of size proceeding clockwise from the top-right, though this pattern is not strictly maintained throughout. No separate legend is included, as all labels are placed directly next to their corresponding segments.
